text:
The Avalanche arrived on a three-game winning streak and left Columbus with it snapped, beaten 7-2 by a Blue Jackets team that scored five times in the second period alone. Charlie Coyle led the way with two goals and two assists, including a power-play tip-in and the seventh goal midway through the third. Coyle was drafted 28th overall by the Sharks in 2010, and he looked every bit the veteran piece Columbus needed.

The score tells less than it seems to. Our numbers rate the game as close: CBJ created 3.66 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to COL's 3.46, and the Blue Jackets "deserved to win" in 53% of simulated replays of every shot, meaning Columbus was only slightly better on the shot map. Colorado actually had more shot attempts, 64 to 50, and owned the second period on chance quality, 1.79 to 1.20. What swung it was finishing. Jake Christiansen scored on a 2% chance, and Cam Talbot stopped 27 of 29 shots, saving about 1.5 goals more than an average goalie would have given those chances. At the other end, Mackenzie Blackwood and Scott Wedgewood combined to allow seven on 24 shots, with Wedgewood giving up four on nine, roughly 2.5 goals more than the chances deserved.

Colorado goes home with its streak gone and a loss that looks worse than the play. Cale Makar and Nazem Kadri did score, and Makar put five shots on goal. Columbus takes a blowout that was partly earned and partly the bounce of a night when nearly everything went in.
